scenes.heading: Expanding and factorising
scenes.say: Can you work out thirty-seven times thirteen plus thirty-seven times seven in your head? With factorising you can! Today you will learn to expand brackets and to put them back.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Unpack 3 bags of (1 apple + 2 bananas): 3 apples, 6 bananas
scenes.breaks: In algebra you can put letters and negative numbers outside the bracket. No negative lunch bags!
scenes.say: Three lunch bags each hold one apple and two bananas. Unpack them and you have three apples and six bananas. That is expanding. Packing them back into as many identical bags as possible is factorising.

scenes.heading: Why expanding works
scenes.say: Here is a rectangle three tall and two x plus five wide. Split it into two parts: three times two x is six x, and three times five is fifteen. So three lots of two x plus five is six x plus fifteen.
scenes.caption: A rectangle 3 tall and 2x + 5 wide. Split it into two parts: 3 × 2x = 6x and 3 × 5 = 15. So 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15.

scenes.heading: Expand and simplify
scenes.question: Expand and simplify 5(2x − 3) − 3(x − 4).
scenes.say: Expand the first bracket: ten x minus fifteen. Expand the second with negative three: negative three x plus twelve, because a negative times a negative is positive. Collect like terms: seven x minus three.
scenes.caption: Expand the first bracket: 10x − 15. Expand the second with −3: −3x + 12, because negative × negative is positive. Collect like terms: 7x − 3.

scenes.heading: Factorising fully
steps: Find the HCF of numbers and letters
Write the HCF outside the bracket
Divide each term by the HCF
scenes.say: To factorise fully, find the highest common factor of the numbers and the letters. Write it outside the bracket. Divide each term by it to fill the bracket. Then check by expanding.

scenes.heading: Factorise fully
scenes.question: Factorise fully 12x²y + 18xy.
lines: Letters in both: x and y
scenes.say: Factorise twelve x squared y plus eighteen x y. The highest common factor of twelve and eighteen is six, and both terms have x and y. So take out six x y, leaving two x plus three.
scenes.caption: Factorise 12x²y + 18xy. The HCF of 12 and 18 is 6, and both terms have x and y. Take out 6xy, leaving 2x + 3.

scenes.heading: Stretch: two brackets
scenes.say: For two brackets, x plus four times x plus three, draw a rectangle split four ways. The parts are x squared, four x, three x and twelve. Add them up: x squared plus seven x plus twelve.
scenes.caption: For (x + 4)(x + 3), draw a rectangle split four ways: x², 4x, 3x and 12. Add them: x² + 7x + 12.

points: Multiply EVERY term in the bracket
Factorise fully: take out the HCF
scenes.say: Quick recap. Multiply every term in the bracket. Negative times negative is positive. To factorise fully, take out the highest common factor, then check by expanding. Two brackets make four products. Now try the practice questions!
